items.title: Jack Sheldon interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: And I work at Chadney’s every Sunday night with Ross Tompkins, we do a duet.

ctx.x: Yeah. So it wasn’t purely just the music. It was the whole spectrum.

The acceptance. Yeah, being in front of an audience and getting the reaction from the people, I guess getting that love, and wanting that love and wanting to play. I was always lucky, I always got to hang around with the greatest musicians of the time. Down in Florida, now when I was started, well Ross Tompkins was a little after me, and he was © Fillius Jazz Archive -3-

down there, and there were some — Bobby Banks, he was an alto player that was in Jacksonville, Florida, and he introduced me to Charlie Parker, which sounded strange to me at first, very strange. And Dizzy Gillespie sounded strange to me then too. I liked Al Killian and Roy Eldridge and Coleman Hawkins and those guys. But then I came to Los Angeles and I got a job at the Central Market downtown, and right next to the Million Dollar Theater, where Dizzy Gillespie was appearing, and Sammy Davis Jr. with the Will…

items.title: Tommy Newsom and Ross Tompkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: The interviewee only responds 'Good for him' to the interviewer's story about Jack Sheldon sitting in with the interviewer and Uan Rasey. There is no evidence the interviewee knew or interacted with Jack Sheldon.

ctx.x: It was the first time in 30 years. He got his trumpet, he went to Uan Rasey for a week, and he came and sat in with Jack Sheldon and myself at the Money Tree last Sunday © Fillius Jazz Archive -10-
night. He said, “This is the first time I’ve played in 30 years.” He got himself a brand new beautiful trumpet.
